I love this game to bits but it's so damn hard to find people to play with.

I am intrigued. What do you like about this game? What makes it stand apart from any other RPG?

I would suggest what I normally do which is hijack long-time D&D players from the local card shop who are looking for something new.

The thing I like most about this game is the leveling system. "Levels" are just skill points you use to train things such as crafting, combat, magic and psychic skills. The combat is nice as well because you use the same system for melee and ranged weapons as you do with magic and psychic skills. every weapon has at least 4 different attacks that you can learn, (the first one is always the basic attack.) The game has 32 playable races, is a classless system, no alignments and can be set in just about any world you want, some notable worlds this fits into are sci-fi, high fantasy, horror and post apocalyptic settings. You also only need to buy one book that basically covers the players hand book and the monster manual.

One small note I need to make is that you will want to print out the table of contents from their website, they forgot to add it to the copy I bought at a fair. Other than that, I enjoy everything about this system.

You've convinced me to check it out. I am always cautiously optimistic of RPGs that shake up the leveling formula. Optimistic because it's a repetitive system that has been overused, but cautious because the overuse of leveling comes from it being a system that works, is versatile, and has been fine tuned for 50 years.
